name: uptime-kuma
one_liner: A self-hosted dashboard that pings your websites and services every few minutes and alerts you the moment one goes down.
buyer: A freelance web developer or small agency managing a handful of client websites who needs uptime alerts but doesn't want to pay per-site fees to a commercial monitoring service.
business_use_cases: A freelancer self-hosts one instance and monitors all client sites from a single dashboard, selling '24/7 monitoring' as part of a maintenance retainer.
A managed service provider white-labels it as part of their client reporting portal instead of licensing a commercial monitoring tool per client.
A SaaS company runs it internally to watch its own staging and production endpoints and gets paged before customers notice an outage.

money_ideas.idea: Offer hosted, managed instances for agencies that don't want to run their own server
Build a public status-page product on top and charge per monitored domain

steal_this: Spin up a managed-hosting business this weekend: $10/month per client gets them their own instance plus a branded public status page — the monitoring engine is free and already battle-tested.
